recommendations.thesis: Lennar trades at 0.92x its own reported book value and Berkshire Hathaway bought $595,294,962 of it on the open market across 2026-09-17 to 2026-10-02 at 76.39-81.96, a Class A VWAP of $79.38, which is 0.875x. The Q3 FY2026 release I read gives stockholders equity of $21,558,959 thousand on 237,756 thousand weighted diluted shares — $90.68 of book per share — against net homebuilding debt of $3,147,136 thousand, just 12.7% of total capital, $1.15bn of homebuilding cash and only $650m drawn on a $3.1bn revolver. That is a balance sheet built to be bored for two years, which is the only thing a 4.98% 10-year actually requires of it. The de-rating is real and so is its cause: new orders fell to 20,879 homes from 23,004 a year earlier, -9.2%. What is not justified is paying less than liquidation-adjusted equity for the second-largest US homebuilder while it still earns a 15.8% gross margin on every house it does sell.
recommendations.key_risk: Four consecutive quarters have MISSED consensus (-9.2%, -1.1%, -3.9%, -13.7%) and orders are shrinking, so book value is not guaranteed to compound — a homebuilder that takes land impairments destroys the exact anchor this thesis rests on. INVALIDATION, and it is not a price move: stockholders equity per share declines in two consecutive quarters, or homebuilding gross margin on home sales prints below 14.0% (it was 15.8% in Q3 FY2026). Either would mean the book I am paying 0.92x for is being written down rather than waited out, and the position should be closed regardless of price. Note also that I am recommending CLOSING BCC today out of the same housing complex; the distinction is deliberate and is in the counter_argument. RED TEAM ADDITION, and it is the thing the invalidation as written nearly misses: total stockholders' equity has ALREADY declined two consecutive quarters - $21,879,376k (2026-02-28) to $21,620,638k (05-31) to $21,558,959k (08-31). Book value PER SHARE is still rising (89.51 / 89.80 / 90.68) only because the share count is falling faster (244,438k / 240,776k / 237,756k weighted diluted). So the invalidation written above is not triggered, but the anchor is compounding on buybacks rather than on retained earnings: if the repurchase slows while equity keeps eroding, per-share book stalls and the only reason to own this at 0.92x goes with it. Watch the share count alongside the equity line, not instead of it.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that every housing asset is the same bet and I am closing one today: BCC goes out at a new 120-day low out of the same end-market. The distinction is the balance sheet and what each company owns. BCC sells commodity OSB and plywood at a spot price it does not set, has no book-value floor to buy below, and shows deteriorating analyst revisions, a -7.7% miss and zero insider buying; LEN owns a land bank carried at cost with 12.7% net leverage and has the largest open-market buyer in American finance under it at 0.85x book. The second objection is better: Berkshire is early as often as it is right, bought six weeks ago, and is barely above water at 83.58 — which is precisely why the entry is an accumulation in thirds down to 77.50 rather than a single purchase at the market, and why the invalidation is written on book value rather than on the share price.

The cut was not the core business: the DICKS banner comped +4.9% while the acquired Foot Locker unit comped -3.6% and swung from a guided $110-150m operating PROFIT to a guided $40-80m operating LOSS. That is a fixable inventory and promotion problem inside an acquisition, not a broken retailer, and management has reiterated $100-125m of cost synergies. Seven distinct insiders then bought $5.59m on the open market at 129.75-136.39 in September with no offsetting cluster of sales, and the tape has begun to agree: +7.97pp against SPY over one month after -25.4pp over three, now above a rising SMA20 143.82 and SMA50 137.43 with the 2026-11-12 pullback coming on the lightest volume of twenty sessions.

DKS reports 2026-11-23, but NVDA lands 11/17 and the whole of retail week (LOW, TGT, TJX, ROST, GAP, BBWI) lands 11/18-11/20, all of it ahead of DKS. A soft read from TGT or ROST takes the group down and the 132.25 stop out before this thesis is ever tested on its own numbers - the one way to lose here while being right.
